text:
Our dead speak to us through the senses

while the marsh breathes,

stinks and splashes,

bubbles and flowers,

offers its berries

and carries the bear.


Like the wind passing over the marsh,

lulling the reeds as far as the eye can see,

so our dead are present

under the water,

in the depths of our soul

the drowned plants sway.


Our dead are rooted in us,

they rest in us,

our soul is heavy with drowned branches

and perhaps fruitful,

perhaps in its hollows something forms a chain

and something invisible to us

offers its purpose stealthily,

which

(what a relief!)

is no concern of ours.

translation.title: Our Dead Speak to Us Through the Senses
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Kilpi's marsh ecology as a way of sensing the dead inside the soul.
